page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft's ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs clocked at 3.4 GHz with single-threaded execution, supported by 128 MB of L3 cache. It provides 256 GB of memory, equating to 8 GB of RAM per core, and bundles a local 1890 GB NVMe solid-state drive for scratch and temporary high-speed storage. Hardware accelerators are not included, with a GPU count of zero.

Benchmark measurements demonstrate high throughput in memory-bound operations. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 449.0 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieved 188.31 GB/sec, placing the instance in the top tier of evaluated systems. This memory performance translates to top-tier execution in PassMark database operations and strong results in multi-core compute workloads, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 20088.0 and Redis SET operations exceeding 61.8 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core CPU metrics fall into the middle tier, and large language model prompt processing for 70B parameter models shows lower efficiency.

Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, integrated NVMe disk, and high memory bandwidth, the E32pds_v6 offers strong resource density for memory-heavy environments. Workloads reliant on specialized x86 vector extensions are not supported due to the ARM instruction set, but multi-threaded database systems, in-memory caches, analytics, and software compilation tasks benefit directly from the dedicated non-hyperthreaded core layout.
description: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 32-core ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V with a dedicated single-thread-per-core configuration, the instance delivers 256 GB of RAM, providing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside an integrated 1890 GB local NVMe SSD. It contains no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight exceptional memory throughput, ranking in the top tier for uncached large-block memory read bandwidth at 449.0 GB/sec and PassMark database operations. Multi-core performance is strong across synthetic tests, Clang software builds, and Redis SET throughput, while single-core processing aligns with median tier results. The absence of x86 vector extensions and lower prompt processing throughput on large language models represent minor operational constraints. This hardware configuration is suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, relational and in-memory databases, Redis deployments, and large-scale compilation tasks requiring substantial memory bandwidth and dedicated compute cores.
